correctness.rationale: The incidence graph is bipartite between originals A and subdivision vertices B. Every open neighborhood of A lies in B and vice versa, so relative legality and eventual coverage of an A subsequence and B subsequence are independent. An A history consists exactly of n−1 originals in any order with n! possibilities, since remaining two originals are connected by an uncovered edge until the (n−1)st choice. A B history is an ordered covering edge sequence of K_n, each edge introducing one or two unseen original vertices; the last edge introduces one new vertex in r(r−1) ways or a new pair in binom(r,2) ways, yielding the stated recurrence. All such histories have ceil(n/2)≤k≤n−1 and shuffle independently in binom(n−1+k,n−1) ways. The extreme coefficients follow ordered matchings and sequential edge introductions. Independent literal graph open-neighborhood DP gave T2=4z², T3=216z⁴, T4=1440z⁵+34560z⁶, but these finite checks are not the universal induction proof.
